summary: The window is dominated by an escalating and unresolved armed conflict in eastern Ukraine, including shelling of a hospital and an explosion at a chemical plant in Donetsk, culminating on the flagged day in an announcement by Russian President Vladimir Putin of a third peace agreement. This kind of high-profile geopolitical de-escalation attempt after weeks of fighting is a plausible catalyst for a shift in market conditions, particularly given concurrent reports of foreign investors pulling capital out of another conflict zone (the Philippines) over fears that violence could derail a peace deal there.
mechanism: Escalating armed conflict near European energy infrastructure and financial markets raises risk premia and volatility; a peace agreement announcement can trigger a sharp repricing of that risk (either a relief rally or continued uncertainty if credibility is doubted), which would register as a regime change in a price/volatility-only model.

claims.claim: Ukraine and Russian-backed separatists were holding peace talks while fighting continued in eastern Ukraine early in the window.
A shell hit a hospital in rebel-held Donetsk, killing at least three people, mid-window.
An artillery shell caused a massive explosion at a chemical plant in Donetsk later in the window.
On the final day of the window, Russian President Vladimir Putin announced a third peace agreement.

Separately, foreign investors withdrew billions of pesos from the Philippines after a deadly battle threatened to derail a peace deal there, illustrating that conflict-linked peace-deal uncertainty was actively moving capital during this window.
The US, UK, and France closed their Yemeni embassies and evacuated staff due to unrest, adding to broader geopolitical instability during the window.

competing_explanation: An alternative reading is that no single geopolitical thread dominates and the flagged change instead reflects a cluster of unrelated business/market items late in the window, such as Apple closing above a $700 billion market capitalization, Siemens announcing 7,800 job cuts, RadioShack's bankruptcy filing, and Pfizer's $17 billion acquisition of Hospira, any of which could independently affect sector-level volatility without a coherent unifying narrative.
